title: The full ocean
hook: as rivers flow into the full ocean without disturbing it, so desires flow into the one at peace (Bhagavad Gita 2.70)
tomorrow: the good news finally comes. so why does your stomach drop?

segments.voice: Six lines back: the left hand doesn't know, where my heart is, my own beam, on the rock, evenness, and yesterday's, steady, not shaken by sorrow, not grabbing at joy. Today the Gita's second chapter ends at the sea.

Stand on a beach long enough and it's strange: rivers pour into the sea all day, every day, and the sea stays where it is. So, yesterday's question: why doesn't it overflow? Krishna's answer in the Gita isn't about water. It's about wanting: the new phone, the next trip, the one more thing. And it's the picture he leaves Arjuna with as the chapter closes.
screen: `RIVERS POUR IN ALL DAY.` → `THE SEA STAYS THE SEA.` → `IT'S ABOUT WANTING.`

segments.voice: Here's the verse, paraphrased. As waters flow into the ocean, which is full and stays unmoved, so desires flow into the one at peace. That person reaches peace, not the one who chases desires. Notice what the ocean doesn't do. It doesn't stop the rivers. It doesn't build a wall at every mouth. The rivers keep coming; the ocean is already full, so they don't push it around. Then Krishna finishes the portrait of yesterday's steady one. The person who lets go of desires and moves through life without craving, free of "I" and "mine", reaches peace. And the chapter's last verse names it: this is the state of Brahman, and reaching it, one is no longer deluded. That's the teaching Hindus take from the close of chapter two: peace isn't getting every want filled, and it isn't wanting nothing. It's being full already, so the wants arrive and settle. And the story doesn't stop there. The next chapter opens with Arjuna pushing back: if understanding is better than action, why urge me into this terrible work? The ocean picture doesn't end his questions. It gathers three days of the Gita. Evenness in the work. Steady in sorrow and in joy. And now full, so the rivers can come.
screen: `WATERS INTO THE FULL OCEAN.` · `IT DOESN'T STOP THE RIVERS.` · `FREE OF I AND MINE.` · `THE STATE OF BRAHMAN.` · then, large: `THE FULL OCEAN.`

segments.voice: Take a glass of water, or wait for your next sip. Before you drink, notice the wanting; then drink slowly, and notice the wanting settle, like a river reaching the sea. Sit with the fullness after.
The full ocean: Krishna's picture of the one at peace, who takes in every river of desire and isn't moved.
Carry this: the full ocean, where the rivers arrive and settle. Thirty days into the old books.
